# Moonsault: Sydney screenshot registration and star/transient evidence dev7

The shared `MediaRasterOps.cls` now supports independently validated similarity transforms (subpixel x/y translation and uniform zoom). Moonsault owns detection, source-time correlation, native full-resolution revisit and short-baseline celestial-persistence validation. Neither the raster nor the Moonsault stage invokes Python or FFmpeg executables.

The 9 November six-screenshot series was fitted to the 20:37:11 Sydney frame. With downtown ROI `(320,315,300,95)` and disjoint bridge holdout `(815,310,240,95)` in common 1316×742 geometry, **20:24:30, 20:32:05, 20:32:17 and 20:37:11** passed the two-landmark gate. **20:17:25 and 22:08:42 failed** and are barred from astrometric inference in this run. The 22:08 frame has a provisional `scale=1.002`, `dx=-2.25`, `dy=-2.75` pixel transform, but independent bridge residual 0.141 exceeds 0.125 gate.

At the 22:08:42 screenshot, 97 coarse positive-change pixels aggregated into seven clusters. Native-resolution 1316×742 point morphology rejected all seven as noncompact or diffuse. At the four qualified time points, the only point-like positive transient appeared at 20:32:17 near `(218,178)` in the common 1316×742 geometry, corresponding to roughly `(318,259)` in the original 1920×1080 screenshot — the known aircraft-streak area. The point is not seen 12 seconds earlier: local contrast 3.58 vs 182.72 levels. `corroborateShortInterval` correctly returns `TRANSIENT_REJECTED`.

**No catalogue star identity or celestial heading is certified by dev7.** Static landmarks can register imperfect screenshots without solving lens distortion, rolling shutter, nonuniform cloud transmittance or real 3-D parallax. The 50% absolute mask is a candidate detector; absence of a faint star from it is not evidence that the star does not exist. All measurements were executed under ooRexx 5.3.0 r13196. Evidence log and SHA-256 manifest accompany the release; no webcam photographs are committed.
